name: Kadant
headline: Sells worn-out parts for paper and recycling machinery that customers must keep replacing.
what_short: Parts and equipment for paper and recycling mills
what_it_does: Kadant makes doctor blades, rotary joints, syphons and stock-preparation and recycling equipment for paper, packaging and other mills, plus debarkers, conveyor idlers and balers. Replacement parts and consumables were a record 71% of its $1,052.2 million of 2025 revenue, and the rest was capital equipment. A doctor blade lasts from eight hours to two months.
why_it_passed: Customers keep buying worn critical parts even when they cut capital spending, and prices held through every volume fall in the filings.
Its markets are small and specialized, and its parts business earns high returns on the tangible capital it needs.
Parts and consumables, the steadier part of the business, grew to 71% of revenue in 2025.
It kept its cash for acquisitions paid in cash, with no share issuance and no buyback above value.
why_not_now: At $264.15 a share the price is above the whole value range of $162 to $224. A buyer would earn about 3.6% to 4.7% a year on the cash the business produces, below a 30-year US Treasury bond (5.43%).
watch: Organic revenue growth fell from 15% (FY2021) to a decline of 4% (FY2025); most of the reported growth was bought through acquisitions, which earn decent but not high returns.
Threats the analysis carried: mill closures, bundling by machine builders, Chinese competitors, and the graphic paper grades in structural decline (about 4% of revenue).
It features adjusted profit figures and redefined adjusted earnings per share, and its pay is based on adjusted EBITDA.
